Expert breast pathology assessments continue to be necessary in the management of ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS). While initial diagnostic workup may be completed using imaging modalities such as mammography, ultrasound, and clinical examination, expert pathologists play a critical role in evaluating the histological characteristics of DCIS. This is particularly important when considering the potential for biopsy-proven invasive cancer.

The presence of ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) is not always visible on routine imaging, which can delay or even miss the diagnosis if it is present. Furthermore, DCIS may exhibit a range of cytologic and histopathological features that are difficult to distinguish using less-than-advanced diagnostic techniques.

Therefore, expert breast pathology assessments continue to be necessary in the management of DCIS, as they provide valuable information on the likelihood of invasive cancer within the lesion. This is especially important when considering the potential for biopsy-proven invasive cancer or determining the extent of disease.
